title: FragFold identifies inhibitory fragments within bacterial proteins
summary: MIT researchers used FragFold, an AlphaFold-based approach, to predict fragments that bind to and inhibit full-length proteins in E. coli. The researchers experimentally confirmed more than half of its binding or inhibition predictions, including cases without prior structural interaction data.

evidence.tested: The researchers experimentally confirmed more than half of its binding or inhibition predictions, including cases without prior structural interaction data.
evidence.unknown: The institutional report says more than half of predictions were accurate; this is a study-specific validation result, not a general success rate across proteins or organisms.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers computationally fragmented bacterial proteins and used AlphaFold predictions to nominate inhibitory fragments; experiments tested binding and inhibition. The AI supplied structural predictions, not experimental verification.
